title: Microsoft Stock News (Oct 19, 2026): MSFT Falls 1.9% to $529.05
summary: Microsoft (MSFT) closed at $529.05 on Oct 16, 2026, down 1.93%, as a chip-led tech selloff dragged the Nasdaq 2.15% lower.
body_markdown:
## Why Microsoft Stock Fell


No fetched source tied Friday's decline to Microsoft news. According to[StockTi](https://stockti.com/semiconductor-selloff-sinks-nasdaq-2-1-weekly-tech-slide-deepens) , the session was led by a semiconductor selloff, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF down 4.14%, and the outlet said concerns over AI-related financing weighed on growth stocks.


The same report, citing CME data, said December rate-hike odds rose to 74.3% from 50.2% a month earlier. Gotrade covered the same[chip slump that closed the week](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/bank-earnings-and-a-chip-slump-close-the-week/) .


A Microsoft headline arrived only after the close. As reported by[Bloomberg](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/microsoft-scraps-uk-data-center-083110363.html) , citing The Telegraph on Sunday, October 18, Microsoft pulled out of a deal to anchor Nscale's planned data center in Loughton, Essex, a site where authorities told Nscale power may not arrive until the 2030s.


Microsoft did not comment, while an Nscale spokesman said its relationship with Microsoft "remains strong and long-term." This report came after Friday's trading and did not drive that session's move.


## MSFT Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Per[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/investors-questioning-ai-trade-microsoft-210500658.html) , Azure cloud revenue passed $100 billion for the first time, up 41% from the prior year.
- Microsoft said in its fiscal fourth-quarter report that customer demand continues to exceed available capacity, according to Motley Fool.
- The Copilot app had 30 million paid subscribers before its latest version launched, up 50% from a few months earlier, Motley Fool reported.


### Risks


- Microsoft plans about $175 billion in capital expenditure this year, mostly for AI infrastructure, per Motley Fool, at a time when investors are questioning AI-related financing.
- The reported Nscale withdrawal points to power and construction delays at third-party AI data centers, according to Bloomberg.
- The stock trades near its 52-week high, so it remains exposed to the sector-wide swings seen on Friday, when the Nasdaq fell 2.15%.
